promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 8 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: You caught a cold with a fever, so this week is a gentle return, not a catch-up. Start lower than where you left off and build back only if the cough clears.

flags.title: Returning from a fever
flags.detail: still coughing and congested on Sunday, so the first run is shorter and easier than the plan was last week.

flags.title: Missed two sessions
flags.detail: Wed and Sat did not happen because of illness, and they will not be made up.

flags.title: Sleep down to 6 hrs
flags.detail: low sleep slows recovery from a bug, so keep rest days as full rest.

flags.title: Felt wiped out
flags.detail: if that feeling carries into Monday, swap the run for a walk and try again Wednesday.

answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer: No, please do not. After a fever you want fewer runs than usual for a week or so, not more, and piling on missed sessions is the fastest way to a setback or a relapse. Pick up with three easy walk-runs, starting a little shorter than before, and only build again once the cough is gone and energy feels normal.

new.analysis:
The one run you did on Monday looked fine: heart rate steady around 140, no drift, no pain. Then the cold and fever took the rest of the week, which is the right call. Rest while feverish is non-negotiable.

The race is 8 weeks away and we are in the build phase, but build only works on a healthy base. Trying to hit the paused plan now would mean three runs in a body that is still clearing an illness, and that usually ends in another week off. A small step back this week protects the next seven.

So this week trims Monday to a shorter walk-run, keeps Wednesday at the level you were already doing, and only lifts Saturday a touch if the first two feel easy. If the cough is still productive or you feel short of breath on the easy walk-run, treat it as a walk instead and message me. We can rebuild quickly once you are clearly well.

settingsProposalBullets: Note that illness in Sep 2026 included a fever to 38.4 and a lingering cough, so future returns from illness are handled conservatively.

safetyCallouts.title: Check in with your doctor if the cough lingers.
safetyCallouts.body: A fever of 38.4 followed by a cough and congestion that is not clearing after a week is worth a call to your GP, especially before you push running again. If you get chest pain, shortness of breath at rest, a racing heart on easy effort, or the fever returns, stop running and seek care.
